text:
Unnecessarily overpriced for the OKish quality self-service area as well.
A non-fresh tea which is been kept in a hot container is charged ₹30. Definitely not worth the quality.

Disappointing Quality and Highly OverpricedI left this place feeling highly disappointed. The entire experience is unnecessarily overpriced, especially considering the mediocre standards of the self-service area. When you are paying premium prices, you expect a certain level of efficiency, cleanliness, and care. Instead, the self-service section felt entirely basic and offered an overall OKish quality that simply does not justify the final bill.The biggest letdown, however, was the beverage quality. I ordered a standard tea, only to be served a non-fresh tea that had clearly been sitting in a hot container for a long time. It tasted stale and flat, yet they charged ₹30 for it. Charging that much money for pre-made, stagnant tea is unacceptable. It is definitely not worth the quality they are delivering.If a venue expects customers to pay these rates while doing all the ordering and lifting themselves, the food and drink must be exceptional. Sadly, this place misses the mark completely. You can get a much fresher, higher-quality cup of tea at almost any local stall for a fraction of the cost. I highly recommend skipping this spot.

text:
Honestly, I feel 4.5 stars for this restaurant is like unbelievable..

We travelled 40km to eat in this restaurant only to see that it offers food at exorbitant prices...
It looks affordable on menu card but when its lands on your table you are like what kind business model is this...

What they call platter is utterly rubbish and is meant for only 4 people (costs Rs. 2400)...imagine it contains hara bhara kebab and pineapple only to increase the size of the platter (who wants to have it in a non veg platter)..

Ask me about the fish... Hamoor which costs Rs. 400/kg in market, they asked me to pay Rs.1400 for the same...seer fish Rs. 700 per piece...I felt I almost landed in a 4 star hotel (though the ambience of this place was like ordinary)...

Service:
They are not aware what's in the platter and clueless about what dishes they serve...
They dont know the order in which the orderrd menu comes on the table and completely clueless about prices of sea food which is decided by the manager on floor.... yes if he likes you, he might quote you slightly less (may be)...

Lastly, they have branded themselves as a premium restaurant but their cash machine doesnt accept sodexo...

A thoroughly frustrating experience and we came out frustrated yet smiling faces only to be relived that we dont have to visit this place again...

Thank you for letting us leave that place...

text:
Location & Access:
Situated just north of Devanahalli town, this spot is easy to catch on your right when driving out of Bengaluru toward Hyderabad on NH 44. Since it sits on the opposite side of the highway, you will need to take a quick U-turn right after the main traffic signal. There is plenty of dedicated parking space out front, making pulling in hassle-free.

Space & Ambience:
The property is massive. Along with a spacious air-conditioned dining hall, they also have a neat lawn area out back that looks well-suited for small gatherings or private parties. What immediately stands out is the upkeep—the entire dining area is spotless, fresh-smelling, and even the washrooms are remarkably clean, which is always a huge plus on a highway drive.

Food & Fresh Juices:
We stopped here around 9:00 AM. As is standard across most South Indian highway eateries at that hour, only the South Indian breakfast menu was available. Everything was served piping hot within 15 to 20 minutes. A special shout-out goes to their fruit juices: they are freshly squeezed with no preservatives or added sugar—something that is both rare at highway stops and genuinely commendable.

Service & Pricing:
The staff is polite, patient, and attentive when taking orders. Pricing is fair and well-aligned with the portion sizes and taste.

Verdict:
A solid, reliable highway pitstop. Between the clean washrooms, ample parking, and hot breakfast, it is well worth pulling over for if you are heading out on NH 44.

text:
The atmosphere and seating of this place are quite authentic. But unfortunately that is where the pleasant experience really ends.

We ordered butter chicken, dal makhni and breads for main course. The server (who had also taken the order) brought malai kofta instead of butter chicken. Despite the order being very clearly communicated to her.

This could have been accepted as an honest mistake. But when asked to take it back, this lady staff started arguing in a loud voice that it was somehow our mistake. This is simply not acceptable.

One goes to a restaurant to have a good time. Not to be spoken rudely to in front of your family. This individual clearly does not do her job properly. And misbehaves when she is asked for the correct order.

The food barely makes the cut. The items we ordered - Dahi papdi, tandoori roti, butter naan, butter chicken and dal makhni - were all just about average. These are all essentials of any Punjabi restaurant and one expects better.

This restaurant can be avoided. I feel for the promoters here - a lot of thought, effort and capital have clearly gone into running this place. But it’s just not being run properly.

Daylight robbery, charging ₹50 for one liter of bottle and they don't sell the other ₹20 bottles nor give you an option to drink normal water.

I have visited the hotel twice: once for breakfast and once for coffee. Both visits were enjoyable in terms of food and ambiance. However, I faced issues at the billing counter on both occasions. During my first visit, although my payment was successfully completed, I was called back due to a misunderstanding by the billing staff. On my second visit, I had queries regarding the bill, but the staff member’s behavior was unacceptable — she remained engaged in a continuous phone call, failing to prioritize customer concerns and queries.

I sincerely request the hotel management to treat this as a serious concern and take immediate steps to resolve it. Maintaining a respectful and professional relationship between customers and service providers is essential for sustaining business and ensuring its growth.

text:
I found myself back at this restaurant thanks to my friends’ demands, and here’s my updated take on the experience!
This time, I tried the chicken tandoor, and it was absolutely delicious—highly recommended! The chicken tikka with pepper was also fantastic, with a lovely smoky flavour. We ordered it twice because we weren’t quite happy with just one serving 😜
For the main course, we enjoyed butter naan and butter chicken, both of which were excellent.
The lassi was even better than before, with a lovely addition of kesar and badam.
The seating is comfy and cosy, with a Punjabi feel all around.
I’d definitely recommend the lassi and chicken tikka (pepper) as my top dishes.

text:
Craving Punjabi soul food on the Bengaluru outskirts? 9th Mile Dhaba nailed it on our recent road trip! Tucked along the highway, this no-frills spot serves up dhaba magic that punches way above its weight.
The star? Their Amritsari fish—crispy, golden-battered sole fried to flaky perfection, bursting with ajwain, ginger-garlic punch, and a tangy chaat masala kick. Paired with their buttery, tandoor-fresh naan (plain, garlic, or butter— all pillowy soft with charred edges), it was a match made in food heaven. Dipped in their spicy green chutney and onion rings, we devoured two plates guilt-free!
Don’t skip the sides: creamy dal makhani simmered for hours, tandoori chicken that’s smoky and juicy, and lassi so thick and sweet it hits like dessert. Meals are hearty, fresh, and priced right (~₹300-500 for two). Service is lightning-fast despite the crowds, with unlimited refills on pickles and masala chai.
Perfect pitstop for highway drives—rustic seating, breezy outdoors, and that unbeatable dhaba energy. If you’re near Yelahanka or heading to Nandi Hills, detour here NOW. Foodies, you’ve been warned: addiction ahead! 🐟🍞🔥

text:
Visited on 03 Oct 2026 with family while travelling on the highway.

The restaurant had a standee promoting a special dish – "Samaras Special 'A' Dawat (Kabab platter)" – but no price was mentioned on the standee or in the menu. We ordered it assuming a normal price and were charged Rs. 800, which we came to know only when the bill arrived after eating.

This is not about the money. Many travellers and families stop here, and promoting an item without showing its price is not fair to customers – once you have eaten, you cannot refuse to pay. Every item, especially specials on standees or boards, should have its price clearly displayed.

Tip for others: ask the price of any "special" dish before ordering.

Hope the management takes this feedback positively and displays prices clearly.

text:
Beautiful Views, Disappointing Food – A Really Bad Dining Experience at NEKTR

The views at NEKTR are absolutely amazing, and the ambience is beautiful. Unfortunately, the food was nowhere close to what we expected, making it a very disappointing experience.

Here’s what went wrong with almost everything we ordered:

* Malai Broccoli: Loaded with cardamom and so sweet that it tasted more like a dessert than a savoury starter.
* Chicken Coriander Soup: Just chicken broth with barely two tiny pieces of chicken. Extremely disappointing.
* Tofu Tom Kha Soup: Essentially spicy coconut milk with just two micro-mini tofu dumplings. There was hardly anything substantial in it.
* Dark Chocolate Mousse: The worst part of the meal. It tasted more like chocolate halwa than mousse, and to make matters worse, it wasn’t even served cold.

The food was so disappointing that we eventually gave up on NEKTR and walked to the Biryani Zone in the next building for our main course.

While the view is undoubtedly beautiful, a great ambience cannot compensate for such poor food quality and execution. We came expecting a wonderful dining experience but left thoroughly disappointed.

NEKTR has a beautiful setting, but the food definitely needs serious improvement. Not an experience we would want to repeat.

text:
Excellent North Indian & Chinese Food! A Must-Try!

We recently ordered food from this restaurant for a small family function, and the experience was exceptional from start to finish. Everything—taste, quality, service, and value—exceeded expectations.

The standout feature is undoubtedly the quality of ingredients. The restaurant proudly displays the brands of oil and ghee used in their cooking—a rare and thoughtful touch that reflects their transparency and commitment to quality. You can truly taste the difference. The vegetables are fresh, and the food feels light yet packed with authentic flavors. Both the North Indian and Chinese dishes were absolutely delicious, prepared with care and consistency.

Portion sizes are quite generous, making it great value for money considering the reasonable prices. Their North Indian-style samosas are a real treat—crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced inside, and just the right balance of flavor and crunch.

The staff here are equally impressive—friendly, polite, and genuinely attentive. They patiently helped us choose dishes based on our preferences, making the ordering process seamless and enjoyable.

The dining area is clean and spacious, offering comfortable seating suitable for families and groups. The only slight inconvenience is parking, as it’s limited to roadside spaces, which can be tricky during busy hours.

Overall, this is one of the best places around for fresh, tasty, and quality North Indian and Chinese food. Highly recommended for anyone who values flavor, hygiene, and honest cooking!

text:
Good food and a pleasing ambience can draw customers in but poor service can undo all of it. That is precisely what disappointed my family and me during our visit to Samara's Veg.
Let's start with the positives. The restaurant has ample parking space and a spacious dining area. The interior has lots of tables and a charming fountain too. I was quite pleased with the restrooms for being well-maintained and clean.
However, while this seemed nice, once we ordered our food, that's when the quality of the place came down a lot. We ordered a plain dosa, poori and a butter masala dosa. When I recieved my plain dosa, I was discontented to find it cold. The waitress then informed me that I had been served the wrong order and we asked to take the dosa back. This was frustrating, particularly because my family’s orders had arrived and they had already begun eating. My family's orders came in time and they started eating but I had to wait for 30 minutes before I finally got my order. Although the dosa itself met my expectations, the 30-minute wait and the mishandling of my order had already soured the dining experience.
This experience left me wondering how crucial good service is to a restaurant's well-being. The food can taste amazing, the atmosphere can look engaging and the location can be perfect. But if the service is poor, the entire experience will not be worth it.
I would kindly request the management team to improve their service quality and ensure that orders are given to the right table. I would also ask them to assure the food is hot and fresh rather than cold.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously so that future diners can enjoy the experience this restaurant's ambience and food promise.
responseFromOwnerText: Thank you for sharing your detailed feedback. We sincerely apologize for the incorrect order, the delay, and the inconvenience caused to you and your family. This is certainly not the standard of service we aim to provide. We’re glad you appreciated our ambience and facilities, but we understand that timely service and serving fresh, hot food are equally important to a pleasant dining experience. We will share your concerns with our team and work on improving our order accuracy and service efficiency. We truly value your feedback and hope to have another opportunity to provide you and your family with the experience you deserve.

title: Samara's Veg Chikkaballapur

text: Visited Kanhaji, located at B-7, SLN Shopping Complex, 842/10, Kogilu Main Rd, Maruthi Nagar, Kogilu, Bengaluru. I tried their Butter Pav Bhaji, which cost 115 INR. The flavor was moderate—neither overly impressive nor disappointing. I also sampled the Butter Masala Dosa priced at 70 INR, but I was surprised to notice that they didn’t seem to use actual butter; it tasted more like a regular dosa cooked in oil. The overall taste was just average and didn’t meet my expectations. Even after inquiring about the lack of butter, the staff insisted that they had indeed used butter, which felt misleading. Additionally, I decided to try their tea, which cost 15 INR, but I would recommend skipping it. The tea was quite watery and lacked any real flavor. As for parking, it's possible to park bikes along the street, but I would advise against bringing a car since there is no parking available on the main road, making it inconvenient for those driving.

May totally knock out this "Kapoor's"

text:
Panchami Garden is a good option for a quick, affordable meal. The food tastes good, though not exceptional, and the menu is quite extensive, offering a mix of North Indian and Chinese dishes.

The North Indian meal is a must-try and offers a satisfying option. The restaurant follows a self-service model, and there is plenty of parking available right in front, which is convenient.

However, the place can get quite chaotic during peak hours when there are a lot of people. My main disappointment was the rude behaviour of the kitchen staff who prepare and hand over the food at the counter. A little courtesy and better customer handling would significantly improve the experience.

Overall, good food, a wide menu and convenient parking, but service etiquette needs improvement. Four stars for the food and value, with one star lost due to the staff's behaviour.

text:
Extremely disappointing experience!
We have been visiting Andhra Vindhu since last year for its authentic Andhra taste, but today every single non-veg dish was bland and tasteless—Karivepaku Chicken, Prawns, Gongura Mutton and Fish Curry. Not one had proper salt or spices, and the flavours had not penetrated the meat or fish.
Management, this is basic Andhra cooking! If customers wanted bland, diet food, we could eat at home. We come here for the authentic, spicy Andhra flavours.
Please seriously question the cook and your quality control. When every dish is under-seasoned, it is not a one-off mistake—it is a clear failure in the kitchen. Don’t compromise the taste that brought your regular customers back. You have spoiled our birthday celebration.

Edamame and Truffle Dumpling was something that we personally didn’t enjoy.

Drinks were average. We got the Match-Mel Boba Tea and N&M ice blended Milo.

Mr Sifat waited on our table and he was an absolute delight!

Overall, a recommended place !

text:
Delicious Food, Worth the Wait (But Bring Water!)
​I recently visited Ananth Andhra Style Family Restaurant and had a very enjoyable experience overall, which earns a solid four stars.
​The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the flavor and quality of the food. Everything was exceptionally well-prepared and the ingredients tasted fresh. The chef clearly knows their way around a kitchen because the taste profiles were complex and absolutely delicious.
​However, a couple of minor points prevented a full five-star rating. Firstly, the preparation time was quite long. We had to wait a noticeable amount of time for our order, so it's something to keep in mind if you visit during a busy period or are in a hurry.
​Secondly, a heads-up to those sensitive to heat: the food was a bit spicier than anticipated! While I enjoy spice, some of the dishes had a kick that might be too much for others. A little warning on the menu or a slightly dialed-back heat level would be appreciated.
​Overall, the superb taste of the food makes this place worth a visit, especially if you have time to spare!

text:
⭐ 1/5 — Extremely disappointing breakfast buffet

I normally never write bad reviews for restaurants, but my experience at Itihas today was bad enough that I genuinely felt people should know before spending their money here.

I went for the non-veg breakfast buffet, which was around ₹300. The price itself isn’t the issue — you can charge ₹300, ₹600, or even ₹800, but the quality of the food should at least be acceptable.

The fish had a very unpleasant smell, and the chicken was honestly one of the worst-tasting chicken dishes I’ve ever had. The overall quality of the food was extremely disappointing. There was dosa, set dosa and a few other items, but the buffet had very little variety, and there wasn’t even a basic juice option.

Calling this a breakfast buffet feels misleading when the selection is so limited and the food quality is this poor. It’s not about the price; it’s about value and basic food quality.

If the restaurant wants to charge more, that’s completely fine — make it ₹600 or ₹800, but serve food that is actually worth eating.

Unfortunately, based on today’s experience, I won’t be visiting Itihas again, and I would strongly suggest checking the buffet before committing to it.

Absolutely amazing experience at Nasi and Mee!

The place has a cozy seating setup both indoors and outdoors, beautifully surrounded by greenery, which adds to the overall charm.

The food was outstanding—we tried the dumplings and they were incredibly juicy and bursting with flavor.

The prawns were perfectly cooked and delicious, and the famous nasi goreng definitely lived up to the hype.

The service was equally impressive. Mr. Siyad, who attended our table, did a fantastic job—very attentive and courteous throughout.

A perfect spot for great food, ambience, and service. Highly recommended!

text:
"Had a wonderful dining experience at Thamaq Multicuisine Restaurant on Bagalur Main Road. The place boasts a spacious, eye-catching ambiance with neat interiors and plenty of parking space, making it a great spot for families and groups.
We tried a mix of their Arabic specialties and starters, and the flavors were genuinely impressive—the grill and chicken dishes were juicy, well-marinated, and cooked to perfection. Portion sizes are quite generous for the pricing, giving you good value for money.
The only minor drawback was the service speed, which got a bit sluggish during peak hours, and a couple of items we wanted were sold out. However, the polite staff and the delicious food more than made up for it. Finishing the meal with their hot lemon tea was absolute perfection.
A solid 4-star spot in Yelahanka for Arabic and multi-cuisine food lovers. Will definitely visit again!"

text:
The ambience was good, but the food was extremely disappointing. The food contained excessive oil, and the quality of the oil seemed very poor, which upset our health.

The curries they served were overloaded with coriander seeds, making us difficult to eat. The taste was completely disappointing, and the overall food quality was nowhere near what we expected.

To make matters worse, most of the items listed on the menu were not available, leaving us with very limited options. The entire experience was not worth the money at all. It felt like a complete waste of money.

Despite the good ambience, the poor food quality, excessive oil, curries overloaded with coriander, and lack of menu availability made this a very unpleasant experience. I would not recommend this place to anyone.

text:
Good food, disappointing service!

Visited Thamaq for dinner today and ordered Dal Tadka, Tandoori Roti and a Pineapple Murukku Sarbath. The food was good, and the Dal Tadka and rotis were satisfying. A special shout-out to the Pineapple Murukku Sarbath, a Kerala-style drink that was absolutely amazing and definitely worth trying!
Unfortunately, the service and hygiene need serious improvement. I had to ask three times for onions and chutney. When they finally arrived, they were served in a steel bowl that didn't look hygienic, with a tiny piece of lemon and a disappointingly small quantity of accompaniments. There was no salt, pepper, spoon or fork available on the table either.
The most frustrating experience was with the billing. While I was still eating, the waitress brought the bill to my table. I ignored it and continued with my meal. Barely a minute later, she returned and reminded me, "Sir, your bill." I had to ask whether I could at least finish my dinner before being asked to pay. She then told me to continue eating. Bringing the bill while a customer is still eating is one thing, but repeatedly reminding them to pay before they've finished is simply poor service.
On the positive side, the food is tasty, the restaurant attracts a good crowd, parking is plentiful, and it stays open until late at night. The overall hygiene is a little questionable but manageable.
My verdict: Thamaq has the food and location to attract customers, but the staff needs proper training in hospitality, service etiquette and basic table hygiene. Good food can bring customers in, but poor service can just as easily drive them away.
I'm giving 3 stars: one star deducted for staff behaviour and another for poor service and hygiene.

text:
We recently placed a bulk order at this restaurant for our team of 15, planning ahead for a smooth evening dinner pickup after a long workday. I called a full day in advance to place the order, large varieties and generous quantities, including chicken biryani as the highlight, with portions calculated for 20 people to ensure everyone got plenty. We even followed up with another call 30 minutes before arriving, confirming we'd be there shortly. Despite all this foresight, we ended up waiting nearly an hour just to get our hands on the food. The staff seemed completely unprepared, scrambling around as if it was a last-minute walk-in.

To make matters worse, quality was shockingly subpar. Several chicken biryani packets arrived with zero chicken pieces, just plain rice pretending to be biryani. Portions across the board were laughably small; what was meant to feed 20 barely stretched to our group of 15, forcing us to supplement with cafeteria leftovers to avoid hungry teammates. The veg curries were drowned in watery gravy that tasted identical to the chicken gravy, no distinct flavors, just bland mush. They even swapped promised chicken dishes with random paneer, kaju, and vegetable kurma without a heads-up or apology, leaving us short on protein for a meat-heavy order.

Pricing felt like a total rip-off for such meager, disappointing quantities way overpriced compared to nearby spots that deliver reliably. Food taste? Strictly average at best, nothing memorable or crave-worthy. Service was the real dealbreaker: disorganized, unresponsive, and utterly poor from start to finish. Save your time, money, and frustration, plenty of better restaurants nearby nail bulk orders without the hassle. Won't be back, and I strongly advise steering clear. 1/5 stars.

All of our guests, thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance, cuisine, and service.

We will enthusiastically recommend Acre to our associates.

text:
I had a very disappointing experience at this restaurant.

The hygiene standards were worse. The washroom was very poorly maintained and had a terrible smell. I could barely stand inside for a minute because of the smell. The wash area was also dirty, with food particles left around. For a restaurant, maintaining cleanliness in these areas should be a basic priority.

I brought the issue to the attention of the billing counter, but the response was that there was a shortage of water. If water is unavailable to maintain basic sanitation, the washroom should be closed temporarily or the restaurant should make alternative arrangements. Simply continuing to operate with such poor hygiene is not acceptable.

I also had stomach issues the following day. I cannot conclusively attribute this to the food, but given the overall experience, it was understandably concerning.

The combination of disappointing food, blood in the chicken and extremely poor hygiene made this a very unpleasant experience. I would not recommend this restaurant.

text:
⭐️ 1-Star Review – Very Disappointing Experience

We visited Acre Bar & Restaurant on Sunday with our group and had a very disappointing experience.

Our total bill was ₹41,133. After making the payment at around 9:45 PM, the staff’s behaviour became very unprofessional. We were not given proper answers to our questions, and the staff did not respond respectfully.

One staff member, Rakesh, was also giving incorrect information regarding another staff member’s name, which created unnecessary confusion.

We were also expecting music/DJ entertainment, but there was no DJ or proper music today (Sunday). When we asked about it, we did not receive a proper response.

For a restaurant where customers are spending ₹41,133, we expected much better service, communication, and behaviour from the staff. Unfortunately, the experience after payment was particularly disappointing.

Management should seriously look into the staff behaviour and customer service. Paying a high bill does not mean customers should be treated without proper respect or attention.

Overall: Very disappointing service and behaviour. I would not recommend this experience.
